doc.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: American bands in Europe and meeting Helen Oakley in 1937
summary: Black musicians touring Europe, and Dance's introduction through Jazz Hot to Helen Oakley, whose record sessions he attended in New York.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well jazz hadn’t sort of — jazz had been a novelty rather in Europe. But once you got into the 30s, you had these big ones coming, Fats Waller here, and Duke and I remember Lunceford came before World War II. I missed him. Calloway, Cab Calloway I think toured. And then of course there had been jazz musicians like Sidney Bechet and Tommy Ladnier and Lord Hopkins. They’d been to Europe with different groups and shows and things like that. But when I got to New York in ‘37, I’d been writing for the French magazine, Hugh Panassie’s magazine, Jazz Hot. And I had an introduction to one of their American correspondents, Helen Oakley, who was making records for Irving Mills at that time. And so that was a very big part of my visit, that at night I could go out and hear the bands that was at the Savoy Ballroom and places like that. In the afternoon I could go to her record session, which was a very — she’d come from Chicago and she knew the scene much better than I did of course.
